A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same LeCoDe benchmark study. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, legal-consultation experiments, SFT comparisons, and user-simulator evaluations, including Tables 3, 4, 6, and 7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and Appendices C and G.

M1.justification: The user–expert simulation framework and Direct SFT, Key-fact SFT, and Key-fact-e SFT procedures remain unchanged in Sections 3.1 and 3.5 and Appendix D.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same Chinese legal-consultation coverage across criminal, civil, and administrative law and the same clarification and advice tasks. Generalizing the source name from Douyin to Chinese short-video platforms does not document added or removed data coverage.

E2.justification: The general and legal-domain LLMs, MediQ, and SFT comparisons in Table 3 are unchanged. The user-simulator and few-shot comparator sets in Tables 4, 6, and 7 also remain identical.

E3.justification: Both retain the 8:2 train/test split, two few-shot demonstrations, ten-round dialogue limit, evaluation metrics, and simulator selection. Appendix training, generation, and evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The case-complexity analysis in Figure 5, strategy comparisons in Figure 7, user-simulator analyses in Appendix C, and zero-shot/few-shot comparisons in Appendix G are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting, including annotation agreement, remains unchanged. No repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or removed.

E6.justification: Reported values and findings are unchanged throughout, including appendix results. For example, Table 3 retains GPT-4 recall of 35.9% and Key-fact SFT recall of 53.8%; Tables 4, 6, and 7 retain their scores.

T1.justification: The formal dialogue specification in Section 3.1, training-dialogue definitions in Appendix D.1.3, and metric formulas in Appendix F.2 are unchanged. No theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both retain the same principal contributions: the real-world consultation benchmark, evaluation of clarification and advice quality, and empirical findings motivating SFT strategies. Source-name generalization does not alter these core claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of case complexity, prompting effects, and SFT benefits remain unchanged. Appendix B retains the same limitations concerning Chinese legal coverage, emotional support, other professional domains, and remaining performance gaps.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the named Douyin source with unspecified Chinese short-video platforms in the introduction and Sections 3.2 and 3.6, removes the source URL, and deletes 'tiktok' from Appendix E.1. This reduces provenance specificity; implementation settings and resource-release information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the related-dataset comparison in Table 1, and references 1–35 remain unchanged. The revision does not substantively alter positioning relative to earlier research.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to generalizing platform references, deleting the platform name in the annotation instructions, and updating the arXiv stamp. Section organization and the surrounding explanations remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Removing the source footnote and reflowing nearby text modestly changes page breaks, spacing, and vertical placement of Figure 2 and Table 3. Figure and table designs, captions, axes, and legends remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 identifies the video source as Douyin and supplies its URL; v2 removes that identification without supplying replacement provenance details. This modestly weakens transparency for a dataset paper. The methods, experimental evidence, and limitations remain unchanged, with no substantive compensating improvement.
